name: Jens Stoltenberg
role: Norwegian prime minister (2000–2001, 2005–2013), NATO secretary general (2014–2024), finance minister (2025–)
summary: A centre-right Labour social democrat who led Norway's Red-Green government and then NATO. He defends the welfare state, unions and progressive taxation, supports liberal social reform such as same-sex marriage and self-determined abortion, and is a committed Atlanticist who backs collective defence and nuclear deterrence.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He said Allies must invest in defence and that his government increased Norwegian defence budgets.

abortion-legal.rationale: He defended self-determined abortion as a right won in the 1970s and said the woman's rights outweigh a doctor's reservation about referring her.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: He backed Ukraine's right to self-defence under the UN Charter with weapons and training.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: He said diversity of cultures and religions has always enriched Norway and that people should respect each other's different beliefs and traditions.

class-collaboration.rationale: He said he was strongly in favour of tripartite cooperation and credited the strong, responsible employee organisations for low unemployment.

close-ties-china.rationale: He called China the most serious long-term challenge, an authoritarian regime that does not share NATO's values.

collective-bargaining.rationale: He credited the system of wage fixing between unions and employers for a fair distribution of income.

collective-defense.rationale: He said NATO stands ready to defend every inch of Allied territory against any aggression.

decide-locally.rationale: He said it was up to municipalities to decide how to organise services using their local self-government, and criticised centralising decisions in the health service.

democracy-best.rationale: He said undemocratic forces should be met by defending democratic open rights and by using democracy against them.

direct-votes.rationale: He said referendums contribute more to division and strife and that he rarely goes for one.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: He said diversity has always enriched Norway though it tests society, which he expected a tolerant country to pass.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He named climate, with poverty, as the main challenge of our time and said he spent much of his term and a major speech on it.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He led NATO for ten years and as prime minister held NATO membership fixed in government platforms.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He said gay people should be treated like all other people and that he would fight with all strength those who say women do not have the same rights as men.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He welcomed Norway becoming multicultural and multi-religious and called diversity an enrichment.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He said oil activity in the Barents Sea is sound today and his government opened new areas to petroleum activities.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He shared concern about nuclear power plants' environmental problems and said it was inappropriate for his government to support building them in Norway.

force-without-un.rationale: He said international law and a UN mandate were crucial prerequisites for Norwegian participation in Afghanistan, Libya and other operations.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: He said giving up the deterrent without guarantees others do likewise is dangerous, and that as long as others have nuclear weapons NATO must have them too.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He said the state and public sphere are governed by legislation coherent across different beliefs and views of life, and that the state is not religiously motivated.

minority-language-support.rationale: He said Sami children are entitled to learning materials in Sami and promised to look into missing textbooks.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: He warned against commercialising hospitals and against extensive privatisation of the common school, while accepting private schools on a pedagogical or religious basis.

party-controls-media.rationale: He described a free and democratic press and a public broadcaster, backed by press support, as a prerequisite for democracy.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He said his government funded faith training in congregations to strengthen and take care of that part of the cultural heritage.

public-ownership.rationale: He said state ownership and regulation had given Norway viable banks and that he used state ownership for industrial development, opposing blind privatisation.

public-service-media.rationale: He listed securing the public broadcaster and press support as part of the infrastructure of freedom of expression.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: He said his government proposed removing the blasphemy paragraph.

reduce-immigration.rationale: His government opened significantly more labour immigration and he said he welcomed foreign workers, while tightening rules against social dumping.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: He said opinions one deeply disagrees with must be met with arguments, not with a ban restricting freedom of expression.

restrict-technology-exports-to-rivals.rationale: He said exporting advanced technologies such as AI to authoritarian regimes creates vulnerabilities.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: He welcomed the government's decision to keep increasing the aid budget in the global fight against poverty and said aid was a long-prioritised area.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: As prime minister he called the new gender-neutral marriage law something he was proud his government initiated, saying love wins regardless of sex.

separated-powers.rationale: He said separation of powers between the government and the courts is a very important part of democracy and he would not intervene in their work.

social-market-economy.rationale: He described the Norwegian model as private enterprise developed through interaction between the state and the market, with community-paid health and pensions.

socialized-care.rationale: He called the welfare state women's best friend because the community takes over care for the elderly and children that women once did unpaid.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He argued for NATO unity of Europe and North America and as prime minister stood by NATO membership.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He said opinions he deeply disagrees with must be met with argument, not a ban, and defended the right of opponents to organise meetings.

surveillance-ok.rationale: He said fighting terrorism needs police and surveillance alongside prevention.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He defended the wealth tax against its abolition and criticised tax relief for the richest as undermining solidarity.

unions-good.rationale: He credited strong trade unions and wage setting for Norway's fairer income distribution between owners and employees.

universal-healthcare.rationale: He set out Labour's welfare society as giving everyone equal rights to health care, school and care for the elderly.

women-suffrage.rationale: He said he would fight with all his strength those who claim women do not have the same rights as men.
